newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN INTERBANK RATES STEADY, LIQUIDITY HIGH.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN INTERBANK RATES STEADY, LIQUIDITY HIGH.

text.p: Croatia's call money rate remained steady on Friday amid exceptionally high liquidity and low demand, despite regular end-of-week payments, dealers said.
The central bank said the banking sector had repaid all its outstanding Lombard loans.
"Banks' accounts are full, and all banks are positive," one dealer said.
Call money loans, granted at seven percent, made up all new borrowings totalling 25.5 million kuna ($3.8 million), she said. Supply was 65.5 million.
"There was no demand for term loans. Some banks are only preparing to last through the weekend," the dealer said.
The banks had an extremely high 813 million kuna on their balances on Thursday and no shortfalls. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075 ($ = 6.624 Croatian Kuna)
